chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Do not turn your knowledge into ignorance or your conviction into doubt. When you gain knowledge act (upon it) and when you acquire conviction proceed (on its basis).
ai.seo_question: How should one apply knowledge and conviction according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns against the stagnation of knowledge into ignorance and certainty into doubt, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the inseparability of gnosis (ma'rifah) and praxis (amal). This teaching underscores that true conviction necessitates decisive action, a core principle in distinguishing mere intellectual assent from transformative spiritual practice.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 274. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Do not turn your knowledge into ignorance or your conviction into doubt. When you gain knowledge act (upon it) and when you acquire conviction proceed (on its basis). [1]
